item.title: One part of Maryland’s plan for cleaning its air? A more leafy state
item.description: Maryland was 1.5 million trees on the way to its goal of planting more than 5 million native trees across the state by the end of 2031 to help reduce carbon in the atmosphere, under the state's Tree Solutions Now Act of 2021.

item.title: Contractors, customers worried by cuts to Maryland energy efficiency rebates
item.description: As state lawmakers move toward short-term reductions to the EmPOWER program, which helps homeowners pay for energy-saving improvements, residents and the businesses that rely on the program try to figure out what's next.

item.title: Crossover day is here: Like your March Madness brackets, but for legislation
item.description: Monday is "crossover day" in Annapolis, when the odds for a bill's passage fall sharply if it has not at least been approved by one chamber. On crossover 2026, a number of bills are already safe but many major initiatives are on the bubble or racing against the deadline.

item.title: Prince George’s may change Cesar Chavez school name after sex abuse report
item.description: School officials in Prince George's County and Washington, D.C., are considering school name changes after sexual abuse and assault allegations surfaced against the late labor leader Cesar Chavez.

item.title: Trump administration pushes to deport Kilmar Abrego Garcia to Liberia
item.description: The Trump administration is again trying to send the wrongly deported Kilmar Abrego Garcia to the west African nation of Liberia and urging a federal judge to dismiss a bar on his removal, according to legal documents filed over the weekend.

item.title: Supreme Court skeptical of letting states count mail-in ballots that arrive after Election Day
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court’s conservative justices appeared skeptical Monday of the validity of mail-in ballots that arrive after Election Day. The case could affect hundreds of thousands of voters in 14 states, including Maryland, in this fall's midterm elections.

item.title: Charles Otto is remembered, Arthur Ellis is missed and septic clogs the Senate, in political notes
item.description: Lawmakers make some noise about a quiet former colleague, Del. Charles Otto, Sen. Arthur Ellis makes his congressional campaign kickoff, and a bill on septic systems that was clogging Senate progress gets flushed back to committee.

item.title: Airport chaos: TSA agents skip work, security lines expand, Trump sends in ICE to assist
item.description: TSA workers missed work Monday at the highest rate since a partial government shutdown began in mid-February, and BWI was among the airports most affected, with 38.1% of workers calling out from work Monday, as ICE agents were sent in as backups.

item.title: Dead for 3.6 million years, but megalodon still survives another day in the legislature
item.description: The giant prehistoric shark megalodon moved one step closer to becoming Maryland's official state shark Monday, one of a handful of commemorative bills that won final approval from one chamber or the other in recent days.

item.title: Ethics, lead shot, housing and gender identity: Lawmakers plow through bills on crossover day
item.description: The House and Senate churned through hundreds of bills in double and triple floor sessions Monday, but that doesn't mean there was not serious debate, as lawmakers took up bills on everything from gender identity to lead hunting ammo.
